items.title: New York Mayor hails Nigeria’s global cultural influence at independence carnival
items.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has hailed Nigeria for its global cultural influence, saying New York owes much of its success to it. Mamdani spoke at Nigeria’s 66th Independence Day Carnival, where Nigerian diplomats, community leaders and residents gathered to celebrate the country’s independence. The Mayor received loud cheers and drew laughter when he explained why attending the Nigerian celebration was unavoidable. “Somebody asked me if I was going to come to the parade. “I said, ‘I don’t want any wahala, I have to be here!” he told the enthusiastic crowd. Mamdani praised and paid tribute to Nigeria’s extraordinary cultural influence across Africa and internationally. The Uganda-born mayor recalled growing up listening to Nigerian music and said he was excited to see some of the country’s stars perform. “I heard that Runtown was going to be here later, and I was born in Kampala, Uganda, and I grew up listening to ‘From Lagos to Kampala’.”Mamdani also referenced Patoranking’s “My Woman, My Everything,” drawing another round of applause from the audience. He said Nigeria occupied a unique cultural position for Africans on the continent and in the diaspora. “Being someone who’s proud to be born in the continent of Africa, we all look to Lagos, we all look to Nigeria for a sense of self, a sense of belonging as well,” he said.The mayor cited Nigerian food, music and football among the country’s contributions that had become part of everyday global culture. “Whether it’s Nigerian food, whether it’s Nigerian music, whether it’s Nigerian soccer players, we know that Nigeria is a part of our life,” Mamdani said. “When we look across this city, we look at what we love, we know that so much of it was made possible because of Nigerian New Yorkers like you.” Mamdani cited U.S. international footballer Folarin Balogun, born in Brooklyn to Nigerian parents, as an example of Nigerian contributions to American life. He said Nigeria’s cultural influence extended across Africa, describing Lagos and Nigeria as important sources of identity and belonging for Africans. Nigeria’s Consul-General in New York, Amb. Abubakar Jidda, congratulated Nigerians across the 20 states under the Consulate’s jurisdiction on the anniversary. “The first of October reminds us of the courage, sacrifice and vision of those who secured our independence,” Jidda said. He commended Nigerians in the U.S. for excelling in medicine, education, business, science, arts and other professional fields. Jidda urged Nigerians in the diaspora to remain actively involved in national development through their knowledge, skills, networks and investments. “Wherever we live, we each have a part to play in Nigeria’s progress,” he said, urging Nigerians to promote peace, unity and prosperity. Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Amb. Jimoh Ibrahim, said the anniversary challenged every generation to renew its commitment to unity, peace, progress and responsible nation-building. “Nigeria’s story on the world stage is ultimately the story of her exceptional citizens,” Ibrahim said. He said Nigeria’s diplomatic presence at the United Nations has entered a “renewed and consequential phase,” driven by proactive, results-oriented engagement. “Today, Nigeria is fully back on the global stage — visible, engaged, influential and respected,” Ibrahim declared. The ambassador described the diaspora as integral to Nigeria’s global strength, citing its professionals, entrepreneurs, scholars, innovators and community leaders. The post New York Mayor hails Nigeria’s global cultural influence at independence carnival appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Alors que Kiev terrorise la centrale nucléaire de Zaporojié, Grossi évoque la neutralité de l'AIEA
items.description: Le directeur general de l'Agence internationale de l'energie atomique (AIEA), Rafael Grossi, a declare dans une interview accordee a RIA Novosti que l'agence respectait sa neutralite concernant les attaques contre la centrale nucleaire de Zaporojie. Selon lui, de telles exigences ne proviennent pas uniquement de Moscou : « Parfois, c'est la Federation de Russie qui exprime son mecontentement, d'autres fois, ce sont l'Ukraine ou les pays occidentaux qui affirment : "Vous devriez designer les coupables" ». Dans ce contexte, estime Grossi, il est fondamental pour une organisation internationale de preserver son impartialite. Il a explique que cette position pouvait susciter du mecontentement, mais a souligne que l'Agence avait l'intention de se concentrer sur sa mission technique. « Nous laissons a chaque etat le soin de tirer ses conclusions et de definir son positionnement politique », a-t-il ajoute. Les declarations du directeur general de l'AIEA ont ete faites alors qu'une nouvelle attaque ukrainienne venait de frapper les environs de la centrale nucleaire de Zaporojie. Le 3 octobre, le service de presse de la centrale a fait etat de dommages causes aux equipements de la centrale thermique de Zaporojie a la suite de tirs intensifs des forces ukrainiennes. Le communique a note que la fiabilite de l'approvisionnement electrique externe de la centrale dependait du bon fonctionnement de cette infrastructure. Les attaques regulieres de Kiev, toujours pas reconnues par l'AIEA Les attaques ukrainiennes contre les infrastructures liees a l'exploitation et a la securite du complexe nucleaire ne sont pas des cas isoles et ont ete condamnees a plusieurs reprises par Moscou. Selon le directeur general de Rosatom, Alexeï Likhatchov, plus de 750 frappes de drones et d'artillerie ont ete enregistrees au cours des quatre mois et demi precedents contre la centrale nucleaire et sa ville satellite, Energodar, et l'AIEA en a ete informee. Ainsi, le 22 septembre, une frappe d'un drone ukrainien a endommage une station de surveillance radiologique situee a environ 13 kilometres de la centrale nucleaire de Zaporojie et constituant l'un des elements du systeme charge de la surveillance continue de la situation radiologique autour de la centrale. Les employes de la centrale nucleaire ont eux-memes ete pris pour cibles lors de ces raids ukrainiens. En août dernier, une attaque de Kiev contre un arret de bus utilise par les employes du complexe nucleaire a fait un mort et 17 blesses . De plus, le 15 juillet, les forces armees ukrainiennes ont lance une attaque contre un vehicule de service a la centrale nucleaire de Zaporojie, causant la mort de l'ingenieur en chef Alexandre Iakovlev ainsi que de son chauffeur, Dmitri Filippov. L'AIEA prefere toutefois rester en retrait, se contentant d'appeler a cesser ces « actes inacceptables ». Debut septembre 2026, la porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, Maria Zakharova, a condamne le rapport de Rafael Grossi sur la sûrete nucleaire en Ukraine, affirmant qu'il ne refletait pas la realite de la situation autour de la centrale nucleaire de Zaporojie. Elle a qualifie ce document de « politiquement oriente » et a accuse le directeur general de l'AIEA d'eluder la responsabilite de Kiev dans les attaques contre la centrale nucleaire, les meurtres de membres du personnel et les tentatives visant a perturber durablement l'alimentation electrique du site.

items.title: Security forces kill 8 terrorists in Dera Ismail Khan IBO: state media
items.description: Security forces killed eight terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Dera Ismail Khan, security sources said on Sunday, according to state-run Radio Pakistan . The terrorists were identified as those belonging to Fitna-al-Khawarij — a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan — the Radio Pakistan report said. Security sources said that three key terrorist commanders were among those killed and foreign currency and a large quantity of arms and ammunition was found in the possession of the slain terrorists. The IBO was a part of the Azm-i-Istehkam operation, the report added. Operation Azm-i-Istehkam was launched in June 2024, symbolising the national resolve to eradicate extremism and terrorism from the country. President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif commended security forces for timely and effective action in DI Khan. PM Shehbaz said in a statement that the Pakistani nation stood shoulder to shoulder with the security forces in the war against terrorism, Radio Pakistan reported. In a separate statement, President Asif Ali Zardari said the nefarious designs of “terrorists operating under foreign patronage and with the support of local facilitators will never be allowed to succeed”. KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time. The province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS). In response to these incidents, security forces have been conducting operations in various parts of the province. On Saturday, state media reported that security forces had killed five Fitna al Khawarij terrorists during an IBO in KP’s South Waziristan district. On Friday, seven terrorists were killed in the Eidak area of KP’s North Waziristan district during an IBO. On Wednesday, security forces killed three terrorists in an IBO in KP’s Mir Ali. A day before that, in an IBO in KP’s Bara area, security forces killed five terrorists. On Monday, four terrorists were killed during an IBO in DI Khan. On Sept 17, security forces killed 10 terrorists in separate operations in KP between Sept 15 and 17. Earlier in the month, over 20 terrorists were killed during multiple engagements in KP between Sept 3 and 5. On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation . On September 26 in DI Khan, 14 people, including two rescue officials, were martyred and 35 sustained injuries after a suicide bomber rammed an explosive-laden vehicle into a police checkpost and then targeted an ambulance shifting bodies to hospital.

What is fuelling French school protests?
items.description: Protests by teenagers outside their schools have shaken France in recent days, with students blockading entrances to their institutions and security forces on occasion responding with tear gas. The government has said that while the grievances may be legitimate, violence is not and has accused the hard-left of whipping up the movement. Critics have meanwhile accused some police of heavy-handed force against protesters, who are legally still children. More than 5,000 people have been arrested since Monday, according to the interior ministry, while about 735 educational establishments were affected on Friday, the education minister said. While the weekend may see a lull, a major new day of protest is planned for Tuesday. AFP looks at the origins of the movement. – Multiple grievances – The protests affect lycees, the schools where French teens have their last years of school aged from 15-18, the equivalent of high school in the United States and sixth form in the United Kingdom. The students’ grievances are numerous, but chief among them are teacher absences, conditions in classrooms, overloaded school timetables and a school day that can be as long as 8:00 am to 6:00 pm, which some say is excessive. “High-school students — particularly those from low-income neighbourhoods — feel they are receiving an inferior education,” said French sociologist Valerie Becquet. – Origin of the movement – The movement began two weeks ago on September 17 at the Saint-Exupery high school in the Paris suburb of Creteil, in support of teachers striking over a lack of staff and resources. It gained momentum, gradually spreading across the country over the last week. Ironically, as tensions raged elsewhere in France, the situation at the Saint-Exupery high school returned to normal after educational authorities agreed to send additional staff, including a deputy principal and a nurse. “Our grades were slipping. If we had not rallied now it would have augured very badly for the future,” said pupil Abderrahmane, who expressed “enormous” pride at taking part in the inception of the movement. – Role of social media – The protests are being further fuelled by the spread of dramatic images and videos on online platforms, notably TikTok. Students themselves hold up their phones to record scenes such as burning trash cans or police deploying tear gas. Numerous channels, seeking to boost their reach, spread this footage and edit together the most dramatic moments. “With social media, they can offer a narrative different from the one presented in traditional media — a narrative that is not manufactured,” said sociologist Becquet. – Social inequality – France offers all students access to the lycee but in reality there is a vast spectrum, ranging from vocational schools to elite institutions. Despite numerous diversity initiatives, the latter remain dominated by students from white, affluent families with university-educated parents. “There are glaring inequalities among different students and schools, and this is a real problem,” said Becquet. – Political exploitation – The protests have become a major issue of political tension just over half a year ahead of presidential elections with the government accusing the hard left France Unbowed (LFI) of being behind the movement. Senior LFI official Manuel Bompard has rejected the government’s accusations, saying it was “descending into conspiracy theories”. Veteran LFI presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon — who is currently polling at over 40 percent among 18-25-year-old voters — has strongly supported the protests, while calling for non-violent methods. – Police response – Protesters have blockaded schools, set fire to bins and other objects and hurled projectiles at police. But police have also moved to disperse some of the protesters, notably firing tear gas canisters, using rubber bullets and sometimes beating them with batons. After students clashed with police Wednesday in Tours in central France, one young man wounded lost the use of his right eye, the city’s prosecutor said. Numerous videos have gone viral showing alleged brutal conduct by security forces — such as a police officer placing his arm around the neck of a girl during her arrest. But police have also been targets, notably an officer who was chased and beaten and kicked by a group of youths from a school in the eastern city of Belfort. kol-sjw/jj/cms The post What is fuelling French school protests? appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Baril à 116 dollars : au Maroc, la pluie amortit le choc, pas la facture
items.description: Le pétrole s'envole, mais les prix tiennent au Maroc, où l'inflation reste à 0,3 % à fin août grâce à une récolte céréalière qui a plus que doublé. La stabilité a pourtant un coût, selon la DEPF : la facture énergétique grimpe de 29,1 % et le déficit commercial atteint 244,7 milliards de dirhams. Le Brent s'échangeait à 116 dollars le baril le 22 septembre, en hausse d'environ 70 % depuis début juillet, après un pic proche de 132 dollars le 15 septembre, selon la dernière Note de conjoncture de la Direction des études et des prévisions financières (DEPF). Au Maroc, pourtant, l'indice des prix à la consommation n'a progressé que de 0,3 % à fin août. L'explication tient d'abord au ciel. La production céréalière de la campagne 2026 est estimée à 90 millions de quintaux, contre 43,1 millions un an plus tôt. Les barrages affichaient un taux de remplissage de 66,1 % au 21 septembre, contre 32,8 % à la même date de 2025. Les prix alimentaires ont reculé de 1,7 % à fin août, ce qui a neutralisé la hausse des produits non alimentaires (+1,7 %), tirée par les transports (+3,7 %). Le gouvernement a par ailleurs annoncé, le 18 septembre, une nouvelle aide exceptionnelle de 30 jours aux professionnels du transport routier. Cette stabilité soutient la demande. La consommation des ménages s'appuie sur les transferts des MRE (+8,1 % à fin juillet) et sur les crédits à la consommation (+4,5 %). L'investissement accélère : les dépenses d'investissement du budget général progressent de 11,4 %, à 75,7 milliards de dirhams à fin août, tandis que les importations de biens d'équipement bondissent de 20,8 % et les crédits à l'équipement de 30,8 %. Mais la facture, elle, se creuse. À fin juillet, les importations ont augmenté de 15,9 %, à 544 milliards de dirhams, contre +8,4 % pour les exportations, à 299,3 milliards. Le déficit commercial grimpe de 26,5 %, à 244,7 milliards, et le taux de couverture recule de 3,8 points, à 55 %. La facture énergétique s'envole de 29,1 %, à 81,2 milliards de dirhams, et pèse désormais 14,9 % des importations, contre 13,4 % un an plus tôt. Les amortisseurs habituels ne suffisent plus autant. Les recettes voyages (79 milliards, +13,4 %) et les transferts des MRE (74,8 milliards) totalisent 153,8 milliards de dirhams, soit 62,9 % du déficit commercial, contre 71,8 % un an auparavant. L'automobile reste le premier moteur des ventes à l'étranger, avec 107,1 milliards de dirhams, en hausse de 14,9 %, soit 35,8 % des exportations. Les phosphates ajoutent une pression. La facture d'importation de soufre, intrant clé de l'industrie des engrais, a atteint 20,2 milliards de dirhams de janvier à juillet, contre environ 7,9 milliards un an plus tôt, alors que les volumes importés ont reculé de 9 %. Dans le même temps, les exportations de phosphates et dérivés ont fléchi de 7,8 %, à 51 milliards, et l'indice de production du secteur extractif a chuté de 28,8 % au deuxième trimestre. Côté finances publiques, le déficit budgétaire s'est légèrement atténué de 1,6 %, à 58,6 milliards de dirhams à fin août, les recettes ordinaires (+10 %) ayant progressé plus vite que les dépenses globales (+7,8 %). Réuni le 22 septembre, le Conseil de Bank Al-Maghrib a maintenu le taux directeur à 2,25 %, en invoquant des incertitudes qui demeurent à un niveau très élevé. items.title: Bel-Aqua intensifies mental well-being campaign ahead of 15th anniversary
items.description: Bel-Aqua Mineral Water is intensifying its mental wellbeing campaign as the company prepares to mark its 15th anniversary on October 10. On Saturday, the company organised a health walk from Ayi Mensah to Peduase, bringing together individuals and corporate teams for exercise and other activities. Participants later gathered at the Peduase Methodist School for games, health screening and access to psychologists and psychiatrists. Head of Marketing at Bel-Aqua Mineral Water, Chris Addo Sarkodie, says the company is taking the initiative beyond its annual activities by engaging workers directly in their workplaces. “So now moving to corporate Ghana, where we are now taking and bearing the cost of psychologists and psychiatrists into companies where they are meeting with their staff and all that. “And now another leg of it is where we are organising this health walk every year to ensure that people can de-stress and have these conversations because there are psychologists around.” He says the company wants to make conversations around mental health more common and give people an opportunity to discuss the challenges they face. “But we want to make sure that we make mental health a discussion. And that’s the reason why we’ve taken it one step further from organising a yearly activity, of having psychologists and psychiatrists and people coming to have that discussion.” According to Chris Addo Sarkodie, the company is also looking beyond awareness by working towards a helpline that can connect people to professional support. “So very soon, we’ll be launching our helpline in conjunction with some of the mental health facilities. “I don’t want to put their name out, but this is something that, from management level, we are very keen on in supporting Ghanaians.” He says the helpline will be announced once the arrangements with the mental health facilities are finalised. Bel-Aqua Mineral Water will mark its 15th anniversary on October 10, with the mental wellbeing campaign forming part of its activities around the milestone.

items.title: Lockheed Martin vise la sous-traitance marocaine
items.description: Sponsor Platinum du Marrakech Airshow 2026, Lockheed Martin organisera dès le 6 octobre une journée consacrée à l'industrie, avec le ministère de l'Industrie et du Commerce. Le groupe américain veut y identifier de nouvelles capacités de fabrication au Maroc et ouvrir davantage ses programmes aux entreprises du Royaume. Lockheed Martin entend donner une dimension industrielle à sa présence au Marrakech Airshow 2026. Le groupe participera au salon, prévu du 7 au 10 octobre, en qualité de sponsor Platinum. Il organisera dès le 6 octobre, avec la participation du ministère de l'Industrie et du Commerce, une journée dédiée à l'industrie, pour mettre en relation l'équipementier avec des entreprises marocaines susceptibles d'intégrer sa chaîne d'approvisionnement et de contribuer à ses programmes actuels et futurs. Cette rencontre doit permettre aux sociétés intéressées de mieux cerner les exigences auxquelles doivent répondre les fournisseurs du groupe, ainsi que les possibilités de fabrication et de coopération industrielle. L'enjeu dépasse la simple présentation de matériels : il s'agit de rapprocher les capacités industrielles marocaines des besoins d'un constructeur présent sur plusieurs grands programmes aéronautiques et de défense. Steve Sheehy, vice-président chargé des activités internationales de Lockheed Martin Aeronautics, a souligné la volonté du groupe de voir les entreprises marocaines occuper une place plus importante dans sa chaîne d'approvisionnement mondiale. La démarche vise aussi les compétences nécessaires au maintien en condition opérationnelle des aéronefs, avec l'ambition de développer davantage les capacités de maintenance au Maroc. Cette orientation s'inscrit dans une relation vieille de plus de cinq décennies. Lockheed Martin rappelle que sa coopération avec le Maroc a débuté en 1974 avec la livraison des premiers C-130H Hercules aux Forces Royales Air. Elle s'est ensuite développée autour des F-16 et du soutien aux appareils en service, puis du renforcement des capacités de maintenance aéronautique. Sur ce dernier volet, Lockheed Martin s'est associé en 2022 à Sabena Engineering et à MEDZ pour soutenir le développement de Maintenance Aero Maroc. Le projet s'est concrétisé à Benslimane avec le lancement d'une infrastructure de plus de 8.000 m², destinée dans un premier temps à la maintenance lourde et à la modernisation des C-130 Hercules. Un élargissement à d'autres plateformes, notamment les F-16, est envisagé. Dans l'enceinte du salon, l'espace du constructeur accueillera un démonstrateur de cockpit du F-35, qui permettra aux visiteurs invités de découvrir certaines caractéristiques de l'avion de combat de cinquième génération. Des modèles réduits de F-35A, de F-16 et de C-130J Super Hercules y seront également exposés. Un C-130J de l'US Air Force doit par ailleurs être présenté sur le site, aux côtés de F-16 des Forces Royales Air, et servira de support aux échanges sur l'évolution du transport aérien tactique, les missions de transport, le secours humanitaire et la réponse aux catastrophes. Le groupe présentera enfin le système HIMARS, le missile Javelin et la nacelle de désignation Sniper. items.title: From banking to party finances: Alfred Kwadwo Thompson elected NPP Treasurer
items.description: Alfred Kwadwo Thompson has been elected National Treasurer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), securing 2,243 votes at the party’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi. The election was held at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium on Saturday, October 3, 2026, as the NPP completed the election of its new national executive team ahead of the 2028 general elections. Thompson brings extensive experience in banking and finance to the position, having worked with several financial institutions during his career. Banking career He began his banking career at the Agricultural Development Bank (ADB), where he worked in the Foreign Operations Department. Within a year, he was appointed Head of the Trade Finance Unit and the Customer Service Unit before later becoming Manager of Business Development and Marketing Communications in the Corporate and Customer Relations Department. He subsequently joined Standard Trust Bank, now United Bank for Africa (UBA), as Deputy Head in charge of Foreign Operations. He also served as Deputy Managing Director of the National Investment Bank (NIB). Thompson holds a Master’s degree in Marketing from the University of Lincolnshire and Humberside and completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Hull’s School of Business Studies. Advocate for financial discipline Thompson has also been active on the NPP’s Communications Team, regularly commenting on governance and economic issues. He has consistently advocated fiscal discipline and greater accountability in public spending. In March 2026, he warned that unchecked borrowing and non-transparent spending could threaten the country’s economic stability, while urging the government to prioritise value-for-money projects. He has also raised concerns about public procurement, including a sole-sourced contract awarded by GoldBod for laptops and office renovation, questioning aspects of the procurement process and alleging a possible conflict of interest. On illegal mining, Thompson has described galamsey as a national security issue, warning about the consequences of violence associated with the activity. Youth and civic leadership His leadership experience extends beyond banking and partisan politics. Thompson previously served as National President of the Ghana United Nations Students and Youth Association (GUNSA). He also served as National Coordinator for Life-Link Ghana and the International Students Movement for the United Nations (ISMUN). His civic involvement includes membership of Rotary International’s Accra Labone Chapter, where he rose through the leadership ranks to become Chapter President. Thompson hails from Twidan Ebusua in Cape Coast and is a descendant of Tufuhen Moore of Sumpa Fie and the King family of Jerusalem Street, Abowinmu. He attended St Augustine’s College in Cape Coast and Okuapemman School in Akropong-Akuapem. As National Treasurer, Thompson joins the NPP’s new national executive team as the party reorganises ahead of the 2028 general elections. His background in banking and his advocacy for financial accountability are expected to be central to his role as he takes up responsibility for the party’s financial affairs.

items.title: Le dialecte tunisien, mémoire vivante d’une terre façonnée par les civilisations
items.description: Lorsqu’un Tunisien parle aujourd’hui dans la rue, dans un café, dans une famille ou dans un marché, il ne prononce pas seulement des mots destinés à communiquer. Il fait résonner, souvent sans le savoir, plusieurs millénaires d’histoire. Chaque phrase du dialecte tunisien porte des traces anciennes, parfois discrètes, d’une terre qui n’a jamais été isolée du monde. La Tunisie actuelle, souvent présentée à travers sa langue arabe dominante, est en réalité le résultat d’une longue rencontre entre plusieurs civilisations, plusieurs peuples et plusieurs systèmes linguistiques. La langue du quotidien est un musée vivant de l’histoire nationale. Zouhaïr Ben Amor * Le dialecte tunisien, appelé communément «derja» , n’est pas une simple variante populaire de l’arabe. Il est une construction historique complexe où se croisent les héritages amazighs, puniques, latins, byzantins, arabes, ottomans, andalous et méditerranéens. Il représente une mémoire collective qui a survécu aux changements politiques, aux conquêtes et aux transformations sociales. L’histoire linguistique de la Tunisie montre que les langues ne disparaissent jamais complètement. Même lorsqu’une langue cesse d’être utilisée comme langue officielle ou administrative, elle peut continuer à vivre dans les habitudes, les noms de lieux, les expressions populaires, les sons et les structures grammaticales. Comme le rappelle Ferguson (1959) dans ses travaux sur la diglossie, les sociétés plurilingues conservent souvent plusieurs niveaux linguistiques qui coexistent et se transforment au fil du temps. Ainsi, considérer le dialecte tunisien uniquement comme une forme simplifiée de l’arabe serait ignorer toute la profondeur historique qui l’a façonné. La derja tunisienne est plutôt une archive orale, un patrimoine vivant qui témoigne du passage des civilisations sur cette terre située au cœur de la Méditerranée. L’héritage amazigh Avant l’arrivée des Phéniciens et la fondation de Carthage, l’espace tunisien était principalement habité par des populations amazighes. Ces populations ont laissé une empreinte profonde dans la culture, la toponymie et probablement dans certaines caractéristiques linguistiques du parler tunisien. Même si l’arabe tunisien appartient à la famille des dialectes arabes maghrébins, il conserve des influences provenant des langues amazighes. Ces influences apparaissent notamment dans certains noms de lieux, dans des termes liés à l’environnement naturel, à l’agriculture ou à la vie quotidienne. Plusieurs chercheurs ont montré que le contact prolongé entre l’arabe et les langues amazighes au Maghreb a produit des formes hybrides où les deux traditions linguistiques se rencontrent (Chaker, 1995). La présence amazighe est particulièrement visible dans certaines régions montagneuses ou rurales où des communautés ont conservé jusqu’à une période récente des variétés berbères. Mais son influence dépasse largement ces zones. L’histoire linguistique fonctionne rarement comme une séparation nette entre des langues différentes ; elle fonctionne plutôt comme une circulation permanente. Ainsi, certains sons, certaines constructions ou certains mots du parler tunisien peuvent être compris comme les traces d’une ancienne Tunisie amazighe. Cette dimension rappelle que l’identité tunisienne ne commence pas avec une période historique précise. Elle est le résultat d’une accumulation de couches successives. Le dialecte tunisien est donc comme un paysage archéologique : sous la surface visible de la langue arabe contemporaine existent des strates plus anciennes qui continuent à influencer la manière de parler, de nommer et de penser. Carthage et le punique La civilisation carthaginoise constitue certainement l’un des héritages les plus importants de l’histoire tunisienne. Fondée par les Phéniciens à partir du IX e siècle avant notre ère, Carthage a développé une civilisation brillante dont la langue principale était le punique, une évolution du phénicien. Pendant plusieurs siècles, le punique fut une langue majeure en Afrique du Nord. Après la destruction politique de Carthage par Rome en 146 avant J.-C., cette langue n’a pas disparu immédiatement. Elle a continué à être utilisée pendant plusieurs siècles dans certaines régions, comme l’attestent plusieurs inscriptions découvertes en Afrique du Nord. L’historien Augustin d’Hippone, originaire de l’actuelle Algérie mais profondément lié au monde nord-africain antique, mentionne encore l’existence de populations parlant une langue punique à son époque. Cela montre la remarquable continuité culturelle de cette civilisation. Aujourd’hui, il est difficile de mesurer exactement l’influence du punique sur le dialecte tunisien moderne. Cependant, plusieurs spécialistes considèrent que certains éléments lexicaux anciens ont pu survivre ou influencer les langues parlées ultérieurement dans la région. Les contacts entre langues sur plusieurs siècles laissent souvent des traces difficiles à identifier mais bien réelles. Le Tunisien contemporain qui utilise certains mots hérités du terroir ou certaines expressions anciennes participe donc indirectement à une histoire qui remonte parfois jusqu’à Carthage. La langue quotidienne devient alors un lien invisible entre le présent et une civilisation vieille de plus de deux mille ans. La période romaine et le latin africain Après la chute de Carthage, la Tunisie devient une province majeure de l’Empire romain. L’Afrique romaine devient alors l’une des régions les plus prospères du monde antique. Des villes comme Carthage, Dougga, El Jem ou Bulla Regia témoignent encore aujourd’hui de cette période exceptionnelle. La langue administrative et culturelle dominante devient progressivement le latin. L’Afrique romaine produit même certains des plus grands auteurs latins de l’Antiquité, comme Tertullien, Cyprien ou Augustin. Mais le latin d’Afrique n’était pas exactement identique au latin de Rome. Il s’agissait d’une variété régionale appelée souvent latin africain. Cette langue a coexisté avec d’autres langues locales et a participé à la formation du paysage culturel nord-africain. Après l’arrivée progressive de l’arabe au VII e siècle, le latin africain a disparu comme langue parlée. Toutefois, son influence culturelle et certains éléments lexicaux ont pu persister dans les langues locales. Les contacts entre latin, amazigh et arabe ont créé un espace linguistique complexe. Cette période rappelle une réalité fondamentale : une langue ne disparaît pas brutalement. Elle peut perdre son statut officiel tout en laissant des traces dans les langues qui lui succèdent. Le dialecte tunisien actuel est ainsi le résultat d’une longue transformation où chaque époque a déposé une partie de son héritage. Les Byzantins, le grec et la Méditerranée plurielle La période byzantine, qui succède à la domination romaine en Afrique du Nord, apporte également son influence. L’Empire byzantin utilise largement le grec comme langue culturelle et administrative, particulièrement dans ses régions orientales. La présence grecque en Tunisie remonte cependant à des périodes encore plus anciennes, grâce aux échanges commerciaux méditerranéens. La Tunisie a toujours été un carrefour où circulaient marchandises, idées et langues. Même si l’influence grecque directe sur le dialecte tunisien actuel reste limitée par rapport à l’arabe, au français ou à l’italien, elle fait partie de cette mémoire méditerranéenne qui caractérise l’identité tunisienne. La Tunisie n’a jamais été une frontière fermée. Elle a toujours été un espace de rencontre entre l’Afrique, l’Europe et le Moyen-Orient. Cette position géographique explique pourquoi sa langue quotidienne possède cette richesse particulière. L’arabe a une histoire tunisienne L’arrivée de l’islam et de la langue arabe à partir du VII e siècle transforme profondément le paysage linguistique tunisien. L’arabe devient progressivement la langue religieuse, administrative puis culturelle dominante. Cependant, l’arabisation de la Tunisie n’a pas effacé instantanément les langues précédentes. Elle s’est faite par un long processus d’interaction. L’arabe tunisien n’est donc pas simplement un prolongement d’une langue venue d’ailleurs ; il est une forme locale de l’arabe, construite par des siècles de contacts avec les populations et les cultures qui existaient auparavant. C’est précisément cette caractéristique qui fait sa singularité. L’arabe parlé en Tunisie possède une musicalité, un vocabulaire et des expressions propres. Il n’est pas identique à l’arabe parlé dans d’autres pays. Il reflète l’histoire particulière d’un territoire. Le dialecte tunisien contient des mots provenant du français, de l’italien, du turc ottoman et de plusieurs autres influences plus anciennes. Cette capacité d’intégration n’est pas une faiblesse linguistique ; elle est au contraire la preuve d’une grande vitalité. Une langue vivante est une langue qui accepte les rencontres. Elle évolue parce qu’elle dialogue avec le monde. Préserver la derja tunisienne Aujourd’hui, la question du dialecte tunisien dépasse largement la simple question linguistique. Elle touche à la mémoire collective et à la manière dont une société raconte son histoire. Préserver la derja ne signifie pas opposer l’arabe tunisien à l’arabe classique ou aux autres langues. Il s’agit plutôt de reconnaître que chaque niveau linguistique possède une fonction et une valeur culturelle. L’arabe classique demeure une langue majeure du patrimoine religieux et intellectuel, tandis que le dialecte tunisien représente la parole quotidienne, l’humour, les chansons populaires, les proverbes, les histoires familiales et la mémoire sociale. Une identité nationale ne se construit jamais autour d’une seule origine. Elle se construit autour d’un ensemble d’héritages accumulés. La Tunisie est amazighe par ses premières populations, punique par Carthage, latine par Rome, méditerranéenne par ses échanges, arabe et musulmane par son histoire récente, et ouverte sur le monde par sa position géographique. Le dialecte tunisien est peut-être l’espace où toutes ces dimensions se rencontrent le plus naturellement. Il est la langue du peuple, celle qui a conservé des fragments de chaque époque. Comme l’explique Bourdieu (1982), la langue n’est jamais seulement un outil de communication ; elle est aussi un espace de pouvoir, de représentation et d’identité sociale. La manière dont une société considère sa langue quotidienne révèle souvent la manière dont elle considère sa propre histoire. Reconnaître la richesse du dialecte tunisien revient donc à reconnaître la profondeur historique du peuple tunisien. La langue comme héritage et comme avenir La Tunisie contemporaine possède une chance exceptionnelle : celle d’avoir une identité construite par la rencontre. Dans un monde où certaines sociétés cherchent parfois à réduire leur histoire à une seule origine, l’expérience tunisienne rappelle que la richesse vient souvent du mélange. Le dialecte tunisien est le témoin sonore de cette aventure humaine. Dans une conversation ordinaire, dans une plaisanterie, dans une chanson ou dans une expression populaire, il continue à faire vivre des milliers d’années de rencontres. Il ne s’agit pas de transformer la langue en objet figé dans un musée. Une langue vivante doit continuer à évoluer. Mais il est nécessaire de prendre conscience de sa valeur patrimoniale et de transmettre cette conscience aux générations futures. La derja tunisienne pourrait ainsi être considérée comme une véritable mémoire nationale : une langue qui raconte les Amazighs anciens, les navigateurs phéniciens, les cités romaines, les influences byzantines, les siècles arabes et toutes les rencontres méditerranéennes. Elle est une preuve que l’histoire n’est pas seulement écrite dans les monuments ou les livres. Elle est aussi cachée dans les mots que nous prononçons chaque jour. * Universitaire. Bibliographie Bourdieu, P. (1982). Ce que parler veut dire : l’économie des échanges linguistiques . Paris : Fayard. Chaker, S. (1995). Linguistique berbère : études de syntaxe et de diachronie . Paris : Peeters. Ferguson, C. A. (1959). Diglossia . Word, 15(2), 325-340. Marçais, W. (1938). Les parlers arabes . Paris : Imprimerie nationale. L’article Le dialecte tunisien, mémoire vivante d’une terre façonnée par les civilisations est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Shettima: Tinubu saved Nigeria’s economy
items.description: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has urged Nigerians to be “generous” towards President Bola Tinubu, saying the president took difficult decisions to prevent the country’s economy from collapsing. Shettima spoke in Lagos on Saturday after meeting with Tinubu, who returned to Nigeria a few days ago from his annual vacation. The vice-president said he and the president remained in regular contact throughout Tinubu’s time abroad. “We are quite thrilled that he’s back on the beat. Advances in science and technology have made it possible to really have impactful leadership wherever one might find himself,” Shettima said. ‘He saved our economy’ Shettima said Nigerians should appreciate what he described as the difficult decisions taken by Tinubu since assuming office, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy and the unification of multiple exchange rates. “It is absolutely essential that Nigerians need to be generous to this poor man,” he said. “When we assumed the mantle of leadership, our foreign reserves was a staggeringly low $3.9 billion that was not enough to import fuel for one month. He had the courage and the conviction to take power-reaching decisions.” Shettima said the economy was “teetering on the verge of collapse” when Tinubu assumed office. “He saved the economy. I want Nigerians to understand this fundamental truism. We were on the road to Caracas; he saved our economy; he saved the nation from falling into pieces,” the vice-president said. He acknowledged the economic hardship being experienced by Nigerians but said the difficulties would not last indefinitely. “We appreciate the pains Nigerians are going through, but tough times do not last forever; tough people do,” he added. FG rolling out programmes to ease hardship Shettima said the Federal Government was implementing programmes and projects aimed at reducing the impact of the economic hardship on Nigerians. “In the next couple of weeks, we are going to launch e-logistics in the North-West. We are going to run 10,600 electric tricycles to ease the pains of the people in the North-East,” he said. The vice-president also said 300 buses and e-taxis would be deployed to “ameliorate the sufferings” of Nigerians. According to him, Tinubu is concerned about the plight of ordinary Nigerians and has “a lot of empathy for the common man”. Shettima described the Nigerian Education Loan Fund as a major intervention designed to help students from low-income backgrounds access education. He assured Nigerians that the administration would continue to introduce programmes and projects aimed at easing the effects of the economic challenges. Shettima also acknowledged the growing political activities ahead of the 2027 elections, saying the administration would continue to govern while engaging in politics. “Politics is in the air, but we’ll combine politics and governance,” he added. The post Shettima: Tinubu saved Nigeria’s economy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ali Suraj elected NPP NASARA Coordinator
items.description: Ali Suraj has been elected the National NASARA Coordinator of the New Patriotic Party (NPP). He secured 372 votes to win the contest at the party’s National Delegates Conference held at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi on Saturday, October 3. He defeated Salim Bamba, who polled 311 votes, and Awal Mohamed, who obtained 106 votes. Ali Suraj’s election comes as the NPP seeks to strengthen its internal structures and broaden its engagement with Muslim communities and other minority groups ahead of the 2028 general elections. The NASARA Coordinator is responsible for leading the party’s NASARA wing, which focuses on mobilising and coordinating support among minority groups within the NPP. John Boadu was elected National Chairman after polling 2,888 votes, defeating Boakye Kyerematen Agyarko, who obtained 2,408 votes. Former National Chairman Paul Afoko received 790 votes, while Sammy Crabbe polled 41. Justin Kodua Frimpong retained the General Secretary position with 4,486 votes. Daniel Titus Glover was elected National Organiser with 2,964 votes, while Alfred Kwajo Thompson was elected National Treasurer with 2,243 votes. Three National Vice Chairpersons were also elected from a field of 13 candidates. Kojo Fosu was elected First Vice Chairman, Henry Nana Boakye was elected Second Vice Chairman, and Nana Akomea was elected Third Vice Chairman. Boadu emerged 1st Vice Chairman with 3,116 votes, while Henry Nana Boakye, popularly known as Nana B, secured the Second Vice Chairman position with 3,061 votes, and Nana Akomea was elected Third Vice Chairman with 2,981 votes. Dennis Edward Miracles Aboagye was elected National Communications Director unopposed. In the special wing positions, Abanga Yakubu Fuseni emerged as National Youth Organiser, while Hawa Koomson was elected National Women’s Organiser. Mohammed Ali Suraj won the National Nasara Organiser position after securing 372 votes, compared with Salim Mansuru Bamba’s 311 and Awal Mohammed’s 106. Alfred Kwadwo Thompson was also elected as the party’s National Treasurer. The delegates’ conference brought together 7,163 delegates from across the country to participate in the election of the party’s national officers.

items.title: Siguirini : un homme tire sur sa femme avant de se donner la mort
items.description: Un drame s’est produit dans la soirée de ce samedi 3 octobre 2026 dans la sous-préfecture de Tomba Kansa, relevant de la préfecture de Siguirini. Un homme, identifié comme Oumarou Fofana, âgé de 28 ans, orpailleur de profession, marié et père d’un enfant, a tiré sur sa femme avant de retourner l’arme contre lui. Selon les informations recueillies sur place, les faits se sont produits aux environs de 15 heures. À son retour à la maison, Oumarou Fofana avait de la boue sur sa moto de marque Haojin, laissant penser qu’il était tombé dans la boue. Il aurait alors demandé à son épouse, Boh Fanta Fofana, âgée de 18 ans, de lui apporter de l’eau afin qu’il puisse se laver. Lorsque sa femme est entrée dans la chambre, l’homme aurait saisi un pistolet de fabrication locale avant de lui tirer dessus à la tête. Grièvement blessée, la victime a été secourue après que le bruit du coup de feu a alerté les autres femmes présentes. Alors que celles-ci criaient et tentaient de comprendre ce qui venait de se produire, Oumarou Fofana aurait pris le même pistolet et quitté le village en direction de Kobafè. Il s’est ensuite tiré dessus sur l’axe Kobafè-Sinimbaya, succombant à ses blessures. De son côté, son épouse, grièvement atteinte à la tête, a été immédiatement évacuée vers le poste de santé de Léro pour recevoir des soins. Le Dr Amara Oularé et son équipe se sont mobilisés pour sa prise en charge. Cinq balles auraient été extraites de sa tête. La jeune femme est actuellement sous traitement au poste de santé de Léro. Les autorités communales et administratives de la sous-préfecture de Tomba Kansa se sont rendues sur les lieux. Parmi elles figuraient le sous-préfet, le maire et ses vice-maires, les responsables du commissariat central de police urbaine de Tomba Kansa ainsi que les présidents de districts. Après les formalités d’usage, le procureur de la région de Siguiri a ordonné la remise du corps à la famille. L’inhumation a eu lieu aux environs de 19 h 30 à Kobafè. Aux dernières nouvelles, l’épouse de la victime poursuit son traitement au poste de santé de Léro. La Croix-Rouge a également participé aux opérations de secours et d’assistance. Affaire à suivre ! Ibrahima Bougouroun Konaté, correspondant a Siguirini L’article Siguirini : un homme tire sur sa femme avant de se donner la mort est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Probe ₦94.4bn allegedly diverted, unremitted oil funds, SERAP tells Tinubu
items.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has urged President Bola Tinubu “to direct the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF), Abuja and the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) to urgently account for over ₦94.4 billion in public funds reportedly diverted, unremitted, unaccounted for or irregularly spent.” The grave allegations are documented in the 2024 (Volume 2) Annual Report published by the Auditor-General of the Federation on 7 August 2026. According to the Auditor-General, the findings in the report variously covered periods between January and December 2023 and ending on 31 December 2024. SERAP urged the President “to direct the appropriate anti-corruption agencies to promptly investigate over ₦94.4 billion in public funds reportedly diverted, unremitted, unaccounted for or irregularly spent, and ensure the prosecution of anyone responsible where sufficient admissible evidence is established, as well as the recovery and remittance of all the affected public funds.” SERAP also urged him “to direct the MDGIF to submit and publish its audited financial statements for 2022, 2023 and 2024 and ensure that they are promptly forwarded to the Public Accounts Committees of the National Assembly, as recommended by the Auditor-General.” In the letter dated 3 October 2026 and signed by SERAP deputy director Kolawole Oluwadare, the organisation said: “Anyone found responsible should be appropriately sanctioned and prosecuted where sufficient admissible evidence is established, irrespective of status, position or institutional affiliation.” SERAP said, “Every naira identified in the Auditor-General’s report must be properly accounted for, and any oil funds found to have been diverted, misapplied, improperly spent or otherwise unaccounted for must be fully recovered and remitted to the Treasury.” The letter, read in part: “There is a legitimate public interest in ensuring justice and accountability for these grave findings. The findings raise fundamental questions about the integrity, transparency and effectiveness of the management of Nigeria’s petroleum revenues and gas-flaring penalties, involving billions of naira in public funds.” “We would be grateful if the recommended measures are taken within seven days of the receipt and/or publication of this letter. If we have not heard from you by then, SERAP shall consider appropriate legal actions and other lawful measures to compel your government, the MDGIF, NUPRC and other relevant authorities to comply with our requests in the public interest.” “The MDGIF and NUPRC should be directed to publish a clear schedule showing the amounts due, collected, remitted and recovered, the dates of the transactions, the institutions or officials responsible and the accounts into which the funds were paid.” “These findings concern petroleum-sector institutions and revenues over which the President, as Minister of Petroleum Resources, has a particular responsibility to ensure effective oversight, transparency and accountability.” “The President’s dual role makes it especially important that the Auditor-General’s findings concerning billions of naira in petroleum revenues and gas-flaring penalties are promptly investigated and that all public funds found to have been improperly withheld, diverted, misapplied or otherwise unaccounted for are recovered.” “The MDGIF ‘failed to remit ₦26.549 billion (₦26,549,415,244.48) in revenue from the sale of petroleum products between 1 January 2022 and 31 December 2024.’ The Auditor-General expressed concern that ‘the money may have been diverted’, and recommended its recovery and remittance to the Treasury.” “The MDGIF also ‘failed to remit and report ₦12.480 billion (₦12,479,683,553.87) in gas-flaring penalties for 2023.’ The Auditor-General raised concerns about the failure to collect and promptly remit the net revenue generated by NUPRC from gas flaring into the MDGIF Account, as required by section 52(8) of the Petroleum Industry Act 2021.” “The Auditor-General is concerned that ‘the failure to remit gas-flaring penalties creates risks of shortages of funds for environmental remediation and potential civil crisis arising from the non-remediation of environmental hazards.’” “The MDGIF also ‘engaged and paid a consultant ₦3.518 billion (₦3,517,519,272.95) to recover gas-flaring penalties without the approval of the President.’ According to the Auditor-General, ‘there was no evidence of due process or due diligence in the engagement.’ The Auditor-General expressed concern that the money may have been ‘diverted.’” “NUPRC reportedly ‘failed to remit ₦38.610 billion (₦38,610,104,671.31) in gas-flaring penalties collected and due to the MDGIF. The Auditor-General expressed concerns about the ‘risks of shortages of funds for environmental remediation and civil crisis arising from the non-remediation of environmental hazards.’” “The MDGIF also ‘failed to collect and account for ₦12.940 billion (₦12,940,311,072.81) in revenue from 2024 sales of natural gas.’ The Auditor-General expressed concern that the money may have been ‘diverted’, and recommended its recovery and remittance to the Treasury.” “The MDGIF reportedly spent ₦261.852 million (₦261,851,719.18) to engage Transaction Advisors, but the Auditor-General found no evidence of job execution by the Transaction Advisors and expressed concern that the money may have been ‘diverted.’” “The MDGIF also spent ₦65.8 million (₦65,800,000.00) to engage Transaction Advisors in August 2024 without due process. The Auditor-General stated that the action ‘may have violated public procurement procedures’ and recommended that the Executive Director of the MDGIF account for the expenditure.” “The failure to properly account for billions of naira in petroleum-product revenues, natural-gas sales revenues and gas-flaring penalties undermines public confidence in the management of Nigeria’s petroleum resources and creates a serious risk that public funds intended for lawful public purposes, including environmental remediation, may have been lost, misapplied or improperly withheld.” “The failure to remit billions of naira in revenues and gas-flaring penalties, the absence of supporting documentation for several expenditures, payments without evidence of work performed, and procurement and consultancy arrangements without the required approvals or due process also raise serious concerns about the adequacy of existing safeguards over public funds.” “The audit findings reveal repeated failures of basic financial and administrative controls, including the failure to remit and account for public revenues, inadequate documentation, payments without evidence of work performed, procurement and consultancy arrangements without required approvals or due process, and failures to submit and publish audited financial statements.” “Transparent investigation and accountability are especially important where the public funds concerned include petroleum revenues and gas-flaring penalties that should be available for lawful public purposes, including environmental remediation and the protection of affected communities.” “The failure to submit and publish audited financial statements for three consecutive financial years also undermines effective legislative oversight and public scrutiny of the financial management of the MDGIF.” “Section 13 of the Nigerian Constitution 1999 (as amended) imposes a responsibility on government to conform to, observe and apply the provisions of Chapter II of the Constitution. Section 15(5) requires the State to abolish all corrupt practices and abuse of power. Section 14 further provides that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government.” “Nigeria is also a state party to the UN Convention against Corruption and the African Union Convention on Preventing and Combating Corruption, which require effective measures to prevent, investigate and sanction corruption and promote accountability and transparency in the management of public resources.” “Article 9 of the UN Convention requires appropriate systems of public procurement and public finances founded on transparency, competition and objective criteria. Article 10 requires measures to enhance transparency in public administration, including access to information. Article 13 recognises the role of civil society and public participation in preventing and combating corruption.” The post Probe ₦94.4bn allegedly diverted, unremitted oil funds, SERAP tells Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Yemen forces say struck Houthi targets in several areas
items.description: Yemen’s government forces said Sunday they had struck Houthi targets around the country, deepening the conflict ravaging one of the world’s poorest nations and the wider region. The armed forces launched strikes against the Houthis in the capital Sanaa, the northwestern governorate of Saada — one of the group’s strongholds — and Taiz in the southwest, military spokesman Colonel Majid al-Nuzaili said. Yemen was plunged back into civil war in July after years of calm, pitting the Iran-backed Houthis, who control most of northwest Yemen including Sanaa. The government, based in the city of Aden, controls much of the country’s south and east — a region that is larger but much less populated. The strikes came hours after the Houthis claimed an attack on an oil facility near the Saudi capital, where an AFP journalist saw flames and smoke, and accused the Gulf kingdom of striking Sanaa dozens of times. The foes have traded strikes since the Houthis seized all of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and took control of the Bab al-Mandab strait in a lightning offensive last month. Houthi-affiliated channel Al-Masirah TV reported that “Saudi enemy aircraft” hit Sanaa with 26 strikes, after earlier reporting “Saudi aggression” against the Yemeni capital, without providing details on the targets or casualties. Two correspondents in Sanaa reported hearing loud explosions and seeing warplanes firing missiles at the city. In neighbouring Saudi Arabia, flames and smoke were seen rising on Saturday afternoon from an Aramco facility south of Riyadh, an AFP journalist said. While the Saudi authorities are yet to comment, late on Saturday, the Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had targeted an oil facility in Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones, adding that they sparked fires at the targeted sites. The AFP journalist reported seeing firefighters scrambling to extinguish a blaze at Aramco’s Riyadh refinery, located south of the capital, while ambulances and police vehicles were stationed near the facility. The Houthis’ Al-Masirah channel also reported missile strikes earlier on Saturday on the telecommunications network in Saada. The Houthis said Saudi Arabia bombed the Yemeni capital on Thursday night for the first time since renewed fighting broke out between the two sides in July. Hunger warning Hostilities between the Houthis and Yemen’s government had reignited after four years of a fragile truce when Iran sent a plane to Sanaa carrying a Houthi delegation. The flight did not seek authorisation from Saudi Arabia, contravening a practice in place for a decade. Riyadh retaliated with strikes on Sanaa airport, and in response the Houthis attacked Saudi territory for the first time since 2022. Since then, fighting has intensified with the Houthis launching a lightning offensive in which they seized control of coastal regions along the Bab al-Mandab strait. They have also struck multiple Saudi targets including oil infrastructure and the capital Riyadh while also announcing a naval blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea. The renewed fighting has worsened a humanitarian crisis sweeping Yemen, with the World Food Programme warning on Friday that three-quarters of the population was unable to meet its basic food needs. Battle for Taiz Fighting in recent days has centred on Taiz, where dozens of combatants were reported killed on Friday. The Houthis reported 55 of their fighters had been killed, while government sources told AFP that 26 troops had died. The battle for Taiz is taking place on several fronts, including highlands overlooking coastal areas recently seized by the Houthis. While the Houthis have conquered swathes of territory, they have yet to take control of Taiz city, Yemen’s third-largest after Sanaa and Aden. The Houthis also said on Friday that Saudi Arabia had launched 94 strikes against areas under their control in the past 24 hours. Saudi authorities reported a Houthi projectile had damaged a school in the city of Najran near the Yemen border. Riyadh has reportedly requested help from the United States, a call so far rebuffed by US President Donald Trump.

items.title: CityBoy records 150,000 members in Ogun, targets 500,000 by 2027
items.description: The Ogun State chapter of the CityBoy Movement says it is targeting more than 500,000 active members across the state before January 2027 as it intensifies grassroots mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. The Director-General of the movement in Ogun State, Dr Abdulateef Sulaimon, disclosed this on Saturday during the inauguration of the group’s state executives and commissioning of its secretariat in Abeokuta. Sulaimon said the movement had recorded over 150,000 active members within a month of commencing its membership drive, describing the figure as a foundation for expanding its grassroots network. “Within just a month of commencing our membership drive, the CityBoy Movement in Ogun State has recorded over 150,000 organic active members. This is a significant milestone for us, but we see it not as the destination, rather as the foundation for something much bigger,” he said. He said the group, which supports Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, was committed to engaging young people, communicating the administration’s policies and encouraging participation in the democratic process. “Our responsibility is to take this mandate to the grassroots, engage our people, communicate the administration’s programmes and policies, and encourage responsible participation in the democratic process,” Sulaimon said. The event was attended by the APC governorship candidate in Ogun State, Senator Adeola Olamilekan; Minister of State for Health, Ishaq Salako; Special Adviser to the President on Public Communication and Orientation, Sunday Dare; and the President’s Personal Assistant on Special Duties, Alhaji Kamorudeen Yusuf. Governor Dapo Abiodun was represented by his deputy, Noimot Salako-Oyedele. Speaking at the event, Olamilekan urged residents to support Tinubu in the 2027 election, saying Ogun State should deliver at least two million votes for the president. “Ogun State has over three million registered voters, and with this number, I believe we should give President Tinubu at least two million votes in 2027,” he said. He cited federal projects, including the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the Sokoto-Badagry Expressway, the Federal University of Medicine and Medical Sciences in Abeokuta and the upgrade of Tai Solarin University of Education to a federal university, as benefits of Tinubu’s administration to the state. The movement’s National Director-General, Francis Oluwatosin Shoga, charged the newly inaugurated executives to extend its activities to all 20 local government areas, engage young people and build a disciplined grassroots structure for Tinubu’s re-election. Shoga described their appointments as a call to service and commended Yusuf for his leadership and commitment to the movement in Ogun State. items.title: El-Rufai paying for what he did to others, Tinubu an ingrate — Galadima
items.description: A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Buba Galadima, has accused President Bola Tinubu and his associates of ingratitude towards former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, despite his contributions to Tinubu’s victory in the 2023 presidential election. Galadima made the allegation during an interview on the Naija Unfiltered Podcast , where he also warned that El-Rufai he claimed to have warned El-Rufai to go on exile after the relationship between him and Tinubu turned sour. “Tinubu and his people are ingrates as far as El-Rufai is concerned. I’m not the best friend of El-Rufai. In fact, I advised him that he should be careful of the way he carries himself, that he either goes on exile or they will jail him,” he said. Galadima said he had publicly expressed concerns about El-Rufai’s situation during interviews with the BBC and Nigerian television stations. He also claimed to have approached former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Kwankwaso, to persuade El-Rufai against returning to Nigeria after he indicated that he was coming back from Egypt. “I went and met Kwankwaso and told Kwankwaso that he should beg El-Rufai not to come back. These people do not mean well to him,” Galadima said. According to him, Kwankwaso contacted El-Rufai, who initially postponed his planned return before later announcing another date and coming back to the country. Galadima described El-Rufai’s decision to return as an act of bravery, given what he characterised as the ruling All Progressives Congress’ determination to retain power. He alleged that the APC could resort to any means to remain in office because of the consequences its leaders might face if they lost power. “The desperation with which the APC is going, they can do anything under the sun to come back to power, because they know what it entails if they lose power; what they have done to people will visit them,” he said. items.title: Mustapha Hamid misses out on NPP Vice Chairmanship by 31 votes despite early poll lead
items.description: Former National Petroleum Authority (NPA) Chief Executive, Dr Mustapha Abdul-Hamid, has missed out on the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Vice Chairmanship, finishing fourth in a closely contested race. Dr Hamid polled 2,956 votes, falling just 31 votes short of Nana Akomea, who secured the third and final Vice Chairmanship slot with 2,987 votes. Kojo Fosu Boadu emerged as First Vice Chairman with 3,116 votes, while Henry Nana Boakye was elected Second Vice Chairman with 3,061 votes. The result marks a significant reversal for Dr Hamid, who had emerged as the leading candidate in an earlier opinion poll. A Global InfoAnalytics poll released on September 1, 2026, placed Dr Hamid at the top of the Vice Chairmanship race with 18.3% of voter preference. He was followed by Henry Nana Boakye and Nana Akomea, who both recorded 17.5%. Kojo Fosu Boadu, who eventually topped the actual election, was fourth in the poll with 5.6%. The poll surveyed 2,581 respondents across all 16 regions, with a reported margin of error of ±1.9 percentage points. Dr Hamid has held several senior positions in government and the NPP. He served as Minister for Information under former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo from 2017 before becoming Minister for Inner City and Zongo Development. In 2021, he was appointed Chief Executive Officer of the NPA, a position he held until the end of the Akufo-Addo administration in January 2025. An academic by training, Dr Hamid holds a PhD in Religious Studies from the University of Cape Coast and previously lectured at the university’s Department of Religion and Human Values. His defeat comes as the NPP has elected a new national executive team to lead the party for the next four years. John Boadu was elected National Chairman, while Justin Frimpong Kodua retained the position of General Secretary. Daniel Nii Kwartei Titus-Glover was elected National Organiser. The new executives are expected to lead the party as it reorganises ahead of the 2028 general election.

2027: ECOWAS to deploy youth observers for Nigeria polls
items.description: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) says it will deploy youth observers alongside its traditional election observation missions to monitor Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. Serigne Ka, Head of the ECOWAS Electoral Assistance Division, disclosed this in Abuja at the fifth edition of the Sectoral Reflection Series on Elections and Democracy, organised by the Peering Advocacy and Advancement Centre in Africa (PAACA) in collaboration with Legis360. According to a statement issued on Saturday, Ka said the initiative was part of efforts by ECOWAS to strengthen youth participation in electoral and political processes across the region. He said the youth election observation initiative had been successfully piloted in Côte d’Ivoire and subsequently replicated in the Republic of Benin. Ka added that ECOWAS would deploy the initiative in Cabo Verde for its November elections and The Gambia for its December polls before extending it to Nigeria. “Definitely, we are not going to leave Nigeria out in January,” he said. The ECOWAS official urged political parties across the region to open their structures to greater youth participation, noting that young people remained significantly underrepresented in electoral and political processes despite constituting a large proportion of the population. He identified access to finance as a major obstacle to youth participation, arguing that young people would struggle to participate meaningfully in politics without the resources required to engage in the political process. “There are many barriers. There are social and cultural barriers, and we have gender bias against women and girls, for instance. But I think the nerve of everything is finance,” Ka said. “Unless young people can access finance, I don’t think they can do much about political participation.” He said political parties also had a responsibility to create opportunities for young people to participate in their internal structures and decision-making processes. Ka said ECOWAS would continue to promote inclusivity, but added that young people must also take responsibility for demanding greater representation within political parties and electoral processes. Also speaking, the Executive Director of PAACA, Ezenwa Nwagwu, said mainstreaming young people into ECOWAS election observation missions was important for strengthening democratic participation and countering what he described as the attraction of authoritarian rule among some young people. Nwagwu urged young people participating in election observation missions to acquire adequate knowledge of electoral laws and regulations. He warned against treating elections as activities without a governing legal and regulatory framework, stressing the need for observers to understand the rules guiding the electoral process. items.title: Extension de la décharge de déchets de Béja avec une aide japonaise
items.description: Les travaux d’extension du site de la décharge de déchets de Béja, au nord-ouest de la Tunisie, viennent de s’achever, en adoptant une méthode innovante d’enfouissement des déchets élaborée et mis en œuvre au Japon. Cette annonce a été faite, le 2 octobre 2026, par l’ambassade du Japon et l’Agence nationale de gestion des déchets (ANGed). Les travaux ont été réalisés dans le cadre du programme de coopération annoncé en mai 2025 et visant à améliorer la gestion des déchets sur le site en question. Lequel programme s'inscrit dans le cadre du «Mécanisme conjoint d’échange des créditscarbone (JCM)» à l’initiative du gouvernement du Japon et de l’Organisation des Nations Unies pour le développement industriel (Onudi). Il met en œuvre la «Méthode Fukuoka (décharge semi-aérobie)» , une technique de gestion des déchets innovante développée au Japon. La «Méthode Fukuoka» est une technique de gestion des décharges semi-aérobies qui accélère la décomposition et la stabilisation des déchets grâce à la ventilation naturelle. En introduisant de l’air dans la décharge, cette méthode améliore la décomposition des matières organiques et réduit la production de gaz nocifs, dont le méthane, un puissant gaz à effet de serre. Les ingénieurs de l’ANGed ont également suivi une formation à Fukuoka, au Japon, en mai 2025, pour mieux maîtriser cette méthode innovante à appliquer sur le site d’enfouissement qui s’étend sur environ 3800m 2 à Béja. Pour rappel, le JCM, mis en place par le Gouvernement du Japon, vise à favoriser la diffusion des technologies de pointe en matière de décarbonation afin d’atteindre les objectifs de l’Accord de Paris. Ce programme à Béja est la première mise en œuvre de la «Méthode Fukuoka» dans le cadre de la coopération du JCM. Les réductions annuelles attendues des émissions de GES sont estimées à 512 tCO 2 /an. «À travers le JCM, le gouvernement du Japon est ravi d’accompagner la Tunisie dans la mise à niveau et le renforcement de ses infrastructures de gestion des déchets» , a déclaré Saito Jun, ambassadeur du Japon en Tunisie. «Je tiens à adresser mes chaleureuses félicitations et à saluer l’initiative exemplaire de l’ANGed; nous nous réjouissons que la Méthode Fukuoka soit adoptée en Tunisie, une étape majeure qui favorisera des solutions durables, la réduction des émissions et une transition plus sobre en carbone et respectueuse de l’environnement» , a-t-il ajouté. Rappelons que le Japon soutient, depuis quelques années, la Tunisie dans ses efforts pour améliorer la gestion des déchets. C’est ainsi qu’il a aidé à la mise en place, en février 2025, d’un système de micro-cogénération au site de décharge des déchets d’Oued Laya, à Sousse, en collaboration avec l’ANGed et l’UN-Habitat. Ce programme pilote transforme 50 m 3 de biogaz émis par ce site de décharge en plus de 60 kW d’électricité, permettant d’alimenter 500 ménages locaux. Dans le même cadre, un programme pilote a été lancé en avril 2025 à Djerba visant à transformer les déchets organiques ménagers en énergie propre et renouvelable, en partenariat avec le Pnud, l’ANME et l’ANGed. I. B. L’article Extension de la décharge de déchets de Béja avec une aide japonaise est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Imo police locate abducted NYSC members’ camp, IED threat delays rescue
items.description: The Imo State Police Command has identified the location where 19 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members abducted in the state are believed to be held, but security operatives have delayed moving into the area over fears that the camp has been planted with improvised explosive devices (IEDs). The Commissioner of Police, Audu Bosso, disclosed this on Saturday while giving an update on the ongoing search-and-rescue operation. Bosso said security operatives tracked the abductors into the bush before deploying drones on Friday to pinpoint the location of their suspected hideout. He, however, said the security agencies could not immediately move into the area because of intelligence indicating that the camp had been mined with IEDs. “Any moment, we’ll still move into the bush. Yesterday, we were in the bush; we trailed them up to a particular location,” he said. “But at that point in time, we couldn’t move into where the coordinates showed us they were because we ran drones yesterday. And the drone actually showed us exactly their location. “But our predicament is that with the intel we have, the camp is mined with IEDs.” The police commissioner said security agencies were preparing to enter the area with heavy equipment, including bulldozers and armoured personnel carriers (APCs), to facilitate the rescue of the victims. “We are moving in there with high, you know, high-velocity vehicles, that is, bulldozers; we’re moving in with bulldozers and APCs to see how we’re going to rescue these victims unhurt,” he added. The development followed the abduction of prospective corps members travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The victims were travelling in two buses when gunmen attacked them along the Owerri-Onitsha Road in the Umunoha area of Imo State on Thursday. The Imo State Police Public Relations Officer, Henry Okoye, had earlier said 10 victims were rescued following the attack, although the command said the exact number of people abducted was still being verified. The number of victims still in captivity has subsequently been the subject of conflicting accounts. While the police commissioner referred to 19 prospective corps members in the suspected camp, reports citing families of the victims have put the number at 20. The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has also deployed the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations, Shehu Nadada, and two commissioners of police to reinforce the rescue operation. Nadada arrived in Imo on Friday and reviewed the personnel, strategy and operational assets deployed for the mission. The police have said tactical teams and other security personnel are continuing efforts to locate and rescue the remaining victims. Meanwhile, families of the abducted prospective corps members have appealed for urgent intervention, amid reports of ransom demands by the kidnappers.
